introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2023. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.
- Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.
- Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.
- In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.
- If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.
- NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées sans source consultable. Les exemples cités sont des exemples reconnus ; aucune statistique précise n'est avancée. Les faits cités sont à faire relire par un géographe avant toute mise en avant.

Fond de carte du Cameroun (page 4 du sujet) : contour dessiné à la main, peu précis. La carte annotée du corrigé est une réponse modèle schématique produite pour cette édition ; les positions (plateau de l'Adamaoua, savane, Bénoué, barrage de Lagdo, mont Cameroun) sont approximatives et s'appuient sur la géographie connue du pays, pas sur des coordonnées exactes.
Q6(b) : « TWO causes each » pour quatre problèmes (8 marks) : deux causes par problème. Points : 5 + 8 + 3 + 4 = 20, conformes au sujet.

Q6(c) et (d) : les stratégies (ministère du tourisme, parcs et réserves, infrastructures et investissement privé) et les mesures pour l'émergence sont des réponses générales reconnues ; aucune date ni statistique n'est citée. À faire relire par un géographe connaissant la politique camerounaise actuelle.

questions.corrige_markdown:
On the outline map, mark and name each item, and add a key (for example a triangle for the volcano, shading for the savanna, a blue line for the river).

![fig-2](gce-ol-geography-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_2.png)

| Item | Where to place it |
|---|---|
| (i) Adamawa plateau | the high plateau across the centre of the country, between the south and the north (roughly latitudes 6 to 8 degrees North), with Ngaoundere on it |
| (ii) Savanna vegetation | the northern half of the country: the Adamawa plateau, the North region and the Far North (Guinea savanna in the south, Sudan and Sahel savanna in the far north) |
| (iii) River Benue | rises on the Adamawa plateau near Ngaoundere, flows north to Garoua and then west into Nigeria |
| (iv) Lagdo Dam | on the Benue, upstream (south) of Garoua in the North region |
| (v) Active volcano | Mount Cameroon, near Buea and Limbe, on the coast in the south-west of the country |

Marks are given for correct location and for naming; a key must be shown.

**(i) Low level of agricultural productivity.**

1. **Traditional methods and poor tools.** Most farmers use the hoe and the cutlass, farm very small plots and rely on rain, so the yield per hectare is low.
2. **Shortage of inputs, credit and advice.** Soils become exhausted under shifting cultivation, and farmers cannot afford fertilisers, improved seeds and pesticides, so pests, diseases and poor soils reduce the harvest.

**(ii) Poorly developed transport network.**

1. **Difficult relief, forests and rivers.** Mountains (the west and the Adamawa scarps), dense equatorial forest, swamps and many rivers make roads and bridges costly to build.
2. **Lack of money and poor maintenance.** The government has limited funds for the huge cost of building and repairing roads, railways and ports, and heavy rains and overloaded trucks quickly destroy untarred roads.

**(iii) Water scarcity in towns.**

1. **Rapid urban growth.** The number of people grows faster than the supply, and the pipes, boreholes and treatment plants built earlier are too few.
2. **Poor infrastructure and pollution.** Old, leaking pipes, electricity cuts that stop the pumps, the dry season (especially in the north) and polluted rivers and wells reduce the water that can be used.

**(iv) Traffic congestion.**

1. **Rapid increase in the number of vehicles and people in towns** (cars, taxis and motorcycles) on roads built for far fewer.
2. **Narrow, badly planned roads and poor traffic management.** There are few ring roads and bridges (for example the single bridge over the Wouri at Douala), roadside markets and parked vehicles block the way, and public transport is inadequate.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) State THREE strategies put in place by the Cameroon government to increase tourism.

[3 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Creating a Ministry in charge of Tourism and Leisure** to plan, promote and control the sector.
2. **Protecting and developing tourist sites:** national parks and reserves (such as Waza and Korup), the beaches of Kribi and Limbe, and the mountains.
3. **Improving infrastructure and encouraging private investment:** roads, airports (Douala, Yaounde-Nsimalen), hotels and communication, with incentives to investors, and promoting Cameroon abroad through fairs, festivals and publicity.

(Other strategies: training of staff in hotel and tourism schools, and improving security.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Suggest the measures that the government of Cameroon should take to become an emerging nation (NIC).

[4 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Industrialise and add value to raw materials.** Process cocoa, coffee, cotton, timber and minerals in Cameroon instead of exporting them raw, and diversify the economy away from oil and a few farm products.
2. **Improve infrastructure and energy.** Build more roads, railways, ports and dams to give reliable electricity and good transport.
3. **Invest in education and technical training** to produce skilled workers, engineers and managers.
4. **Improve the business climate and attract investors.** Fight corruption, keep peace and security, give tax incentives, and build export industries and regional trade (CEMAC, the African free trade area).

(This is also the aim of the national long-term vision to become an emerging country.)
